title: Stability playbook: weekly annotated log (Apr 11 2029)
body:
Purpose:
This annotated weekly log collects the SRE team’s operational highlights from Apr 4–Apr 11 2029. It is intentionally written as a working playbook snapshot: incident summaries, short hypotheses, immediate mitigations, SLO signals, and explicit handoff notes for next shift. Treat items below as work-in-progress; action owners and follow-ups are listed where available.

Top-level summary (one line):
- Stable overall; two medium-impact latency regressions (global) during business hours, mitigated by routing changes and temporary cache increases. No user-facing error-rate spike.

Incidents this week:
1) Incident SRE-1189 — inter-region latency spike (Apr 8 13:02–13:42 UTC)
   - Symptom: 95th percentile token latency for hosted/text-generation increased from baseline 140ms -> 680ms across eu-west and us-east for ~40 minutes.
   - Detection: alert from latency-aggregator (threshold breach on p95), paging at 13:05.
   - Immediate mitigations taken:
     * Shift lead (Maya) triggered traffic split to regional fallback pools at 13:12 (20% traffic rerouted away from primary pools).
     * Increased prefix-KV cache TTL on hot models by +60s which reduced backend tokens per request.
     * Short circuit enabled on a subset of long-prompts to use a smaller quantized model for non-critical routes.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: cloud provider interconnect experienced transient packet loss compounded by sub-optimal kernel path on a subset of serving nodes. We saw increased TCP retransmits in metrics and a small bump in GPU kernel queue times.
   - Post-incident actions (owner / ETA):
     * eng-infra to validate network path and liaise with cloud partner (Elliot / 2029-04-15).
     * Create a canary for connection-level retransmit detection (alerts) (Priya / 2029-04-20).
     * Add a routing tier that prefers colocated pools for stateful sessions (design doc) (Jordan / 2029-04-25).
   - Customer impact: degraded latency but no failures; support notified of elevated latencies for affected customers.

2) Incident SRE-1192 — autoscaler overshoot causing queueing (Apr 10 09:10–09:48 UTC)
   - Symptom: elevated queue depth on dedicated pools after a synthetic workload spike; autoscaler spun extra nodes but with cold-starts causing GPU warmup delays -> increased latencies for 15–20 minutes.
   - Detection: queue-depth alert + on-call Slack from Dedicated team.
   - Immediate mitigations:
     * Manually increased warm-pool size for affected capacity profile.
     * Enabled warm-up preloads for commonly used models.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: autoscaler scale-in/scale-out hysteresis mis-tuned for bursty synthetic workloads; scaler used CPU-based heuristics that don’t reflect GPU readiness.
   - Post-incident actions (owner / ETA):
     * Revise autoscaler heuristics to incorporate GPU readiness and model cache priming (infra + serving-runtime; Elliot & Hema / 2029-05-02).
     * Add a synthetic-canary that exercises model cold-starts hourly during off-peak (SRE tooling / 2029-04-22).
   - Customer impact: brief latency blips for Dedicated customers; remediation credited for affected customers where SLAs warranted.

SLO snapshot and anomalies:
- Latency SLOs: hosted/text-generation p95 target = 200ms. Weekly rolling p95 = 228ms (slightly above target due to incidents).
- Availability SLOs: 99.95% target; achieved 99.98% for week.
- Error budget: small drawdown (~0.03%) due to latency breach; monitoring shows full recovery.
- Action: we will not trigger an immediate SLO review cycle, but will schedule a latency review with product-hosted-api if p95 remains >220ms after mitigations (Jordan / 2029-04-19).

Runbook and playbook changes proposed:
- Add a new section to the latency playbook for inter-region fallback thresholds (thresholds and decision tree) (owner: Jordan, draft due 2029-04-20).
- Document a cold-start mitigation checklist for Dedicated pools: warm-pool sizing guidance, cache priming steps, and autoscaler signal expected latencies (owner: Elliot, 2029-04-22).
- Update on-call checklist to include a mandatory ‘verify network retransmit metrics’ step for cross-region latency pages (owner: Priya, 2029-04-14).

On-call handoff notes (for next 48h):
- Current risks: expected traffic surge on Apr 13 due to product marketing campaign – prep: increase hot cache windows for top 10 models, pre-warm dedicated pools for known customers. (Action: Maya / 2029-04-12 17:00 UTC)
- Current experiments that may affect ops: A/B test for batch-size adaptive routing active in us-east (feature flag AB-32). If p95 > 300ms in that region, rollback flag. (Owner: Priya)
- Incidents to watch: SRE-1189 follow-up network validations; set recurrent check in PagerDuty schedule for 48h post validation.

Open action items (explicit owners):
- Jordan: draft routing-tier design doc for colocated session preference (ETA 2029-04-25).
- Elliot: implement GPU readiness metric into autoscaler simulation and prototype alert (ETA 2029-04-22).
- Priya: add network retransmit checks into latency-aggregator and update on-call playbook (ETA 2029-04-14).
- Maya: coordinate with GTM to get the traffic forecast for Apr 13 and confirm pre-warm plan (ETA 2029-04-12).

Notes from weekly SRE sync (Apr 11 meeting highlights):
- Observability: new trace sampling knob in staging reduced trace overhead but still captures tail; propose enabling for a small subset of production routes (Maya / trial next week).
- Capacity: Dedicated product requests for guaranteed burst capacity need clearer pricing; Finance to loop in for packaging (Jordan to set meeting w/ finance).
- Reliability experiments: running a ‘graceful-degrade’ policy for long-running function calls — early results show 8–12% token-cost savings without perceptible quality loss (Elliot).

Knowledge and troubleshooting tips (short):
- Quick triage checklist for latency pages: 1) confirm p95 spike across aggregates vs single host; 2) check TCP retransmits & network error rates; 3) compare GPU queue lengths and kernel latencies; 4) check prefix-KV hit rate; 5) consider routing to smaller quantized variants.
- Useful queries: saved dashboards -> "Latency Explorer / p95 by region and model"; saved alert -> "p95 sustained 5m > 200ms".

Unresolved questions and debates (for follow-up):
- Threshold tuning: should p95 target be region-specific? E.g., tighter for us-east infra customers, looser for APAC regional caches. (Next discussion: Apr 18).
- Cost tradeoffs: how much warm-pool capacity is acceptable from a unit-cost perspective vs latency savings? Finance + Product decision required.

Appendix: quick links and references
- Latency playbook (draft): CONFLUENCE-4242
- Incident tickets: JIRA-SRE-1189, JIRA-SRE-1192
- Relevant PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/latency-fixes-pr

If you are on-call next shift: read the "On-call immediate checklist" pinned in Slack #sre-ops before accepting pages; escalate to the on-call lead if two mitigations have been applied and p95 remains > 300ms for 15 minutes.

----
Document notes: This document is an annotated, action-oriented log rather than a final postmortem. Please add any missing details directly below, or add comments inline in the Confluence draft for longer-running design items.
